agent: transport second half, the collecting session
question: When the paradrop asks whether the player is told, and what its take-off does after telling the unit home or finding no way.
slots_noted: CParadropMission slots 13 and 14 are in the record already; this fragment revises only the comments of TakeOff (reached from both) and IsActive, so no slot is offered again.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::TakeOff
addresses.revises: Two things the comment left open, read on a decompile: after telling the unit home for want of fuel or fitness it does nothing more that hour, and the light is judged only where a way was found.
addresses.comment: What starts a drop, from slot 13 and from slot 14 every hour the unit is not yet over its target. Out of fuel (CUnit +0x100 zero) or unfit to fly (slot 25, CAirOrder::IsFitToFly): told to return to base, **and nothing more that hour** - before the order's start hour a unit is never fit to fly, so it is told so every hour it waits. Before the order's start hour (+0x28): nothing. Then, with `enemy` = the target's controller at war with the air unit's owner (CCountry::IsEnemy): for each unit it carries (CUnit +0x2E4), where `enemy` and that unit's attack delay (CUnit +0xD4) is running, nothing - it waits; and for each brigade of each, organisation x 1000 / maximum organisation (CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation; a maximum of 0 counts as -1) under PARATROOP_MISSION_ORG_REQ (military +0xAC, 0.95), nothing - it waits. Otherwise the way to the target (CPathFind::Find, SetUnitPath) and, **only where a way was found**, the light at the hour of arrival judged as FlyToCarrier does; the wrong light sends a unit away from its base's province home, and cancels the movement of one in it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 2026-10-16: `if (fuel == 0 || !IsFitToFly) OrderReturnToBase; else if (start_date <= tick) { ... if (CPathFind::Find(...)) { SetUnitPath; NextArrivalHour; IsNightAtTick; if wrong light: province != base province -> OrderReturnToBase, else CancelMovement } }`.

addresses.name: CParadropMission::IsActive
addresses.revises: The message's test is asked after the drop, so of the controller the drop left; and the once-only byte is set before the test, told or not.
addresses.comment: Slot 14, every hour. No base: done. In a battle, a bombing or with a path: goes on. At its own base with nothing aboard (+0x2EC): done. Before the start hour: goes on. Not in the target province: TakeOff again, goes on. **Over the target: the drop** - CAir::DropCarried; each wing's organisation (+0x60) x PARATROOP_DROP_ORG_MULT_PLANE (military +0xA8, 0.01) / 1000, not under 0; told to return to base; and the first time only - the byte +0x80, saved as `message`, **set before anything is asked** - where the target's controller **after the drop** is the player and the air unit's owner is at war with the player, the message PARATROOPEDUS with ENEMY the owner's name and PROV the province's. So an undefended province of the player's, taken by the drop's own CheckForCombat, tells the player nothing, and never will. Never asks CAirOrder::IsActive, so no range is measured. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3.
